label: A son of the diocese
blurb: Raised here. Your home parish is a real place with a real pastor who remembers you as an altar boy.
outcome: The chancery will read you as one of ours, which is worth more than you yet know. There are priests in this diocese who knew you before you were impressive, and a few who will say so. You cannot be sent anywhere your past cannot follow, and you would not want to be.

hooks.label: The pastor who knew you as a boy

label: You went to school here
blurb: Not from here, but you did your college or graduate work in the diocese and stayed.
outcome: Known, not owned. The university will remember you, and so will a few donors and one or two professors who still have opinions about what you should do with yourself. You are a middle case, which is comfortable and is also why nobody fights over you.

hooks.label: The university where you were a student
A professor who thinks you are wasting yourself

label: You came for the seminary
blurb: An outsider. You applied here from somewhere else, for reasons of your own.
outcome: No history, no expectations, no one's nephew. You will spend your first years being placed rather than known, and every assignment will be a test you did not know you were taking. The upside is real: you will be judged only on what you do.

hooks.label: The reason you chose this diocese, which you have told no one in full

label: You transferred in late
blurb: You began formation somewhere else and came here. People will wonder why.
outcome: There is a question mark after your name in a file somewhere, and it will be there for years. Why did he leave? Some will assume the worst and some will assume you were badly treated, and both will be wrong in interesting ways. Highest variance of any road in.

effects.value: What happened at the first seminary

hooks.label: A rector who wrote a letter about you
